newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-HOCH EXTENDS LEAD TO FOUR STROKES IN SARAZEN WORLD OPEN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-HOCH EXTENDS LEAD TO FOUR STROKES IN SARAZEN WORLD OPEN.

text.p: Consistent Scott Hoch displayed precision off the tee to extend his lead to four strokes after the third round at the $1.9 million Sarazen World Open on Saturday.
"I drove it well. I think that was the key," said Hoch, who shot two-under-par 70 to double his lead in cool, windy conditions at Chateau Elan.

He was at 14-under 202 with one round left, while defending champion Frank Nobilo of New Zealand was alone on 206 after a rollercoaster even-par 72 which ended a run of eight successive sub-par rounds here.
Former Masters champion Craig Stadler (70) was five strokes behind, while two-time major winner Payne Stewart (71) trailed by six shots.
"I'm pleased with where I am," continued Hoch, whose two bogeys were the result of three-putting. "It was a long, hard day. It's very easy for your mind to stray in tough conditions."
Nobilo had no objection to the demanding conditions, but he misclubbed several times to leave himself facing a big final round deficit.
"Scott played very well. He didn't seem to be in nearly as much trouble as I was. He shot 70 very comfortably," said Nobilo, who mixed four birdies with four bogeys.
He was particularly pleased with his birdie at the final hole, where he knocked in a 12-foot putt moments after Hoch had made birdie.
Only nine of 52 players bettered par as the average score skyrocketed to 74.1 strokes.
Former U.S. Open runner-up Mike Donald shot the day's best score, a four-under 68 that elevated him 30 places to equal 16th.
